title: Functorial resolutions on the entire bounded-above category
statement: Let $A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], and let $\mathcal F$ be a class of its objects containing zero and closed under isomorphisms, finite biproducts and direct summands (if $U\oplus V\in\mathcal F$, then $U,V\in\mathcal F$). Suppose there is a functor $P:A\to A$ with $P(M)\in\mathcal F$ for every $M$ and a natural transformation $\epsilon:P\Rightarrow\operatorname{id}_A$ with epimorphic components. Let $\mathrm{CoCh}^{-}(A)$ be the full subcategory of cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] whose terms vanish in all sufficiently large degrees; an upper bound is not part of the data of an object. There is a functor $S:\mathrm{CoCh}^{-}(A)\to\mathrm{CoCh}(A)$ and a natural transformation $a:S\Rightarrow\iota$, where $\iota$ is the inclusion, such that every $a_L:S(L)\to L$ is a quasi-isomorphism, every term of $S(L)$ belongs to $\mathcal F$, and for every integer $b$, $L^i=0$ for $i>b$ implies $S(L)^i=0$ for $i>b$. The functor acts on all maps of bounded-above complexes, including maps between complexes with different upper bounds.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-left-resolution-reduced-class] to the given class $\mathcal F$, cover functor $P$ and epimorphism $\epsilon$; its hypotheses are exactly those of the item ($A$ abelian [def-sp-abelian]; $\mathcal F$ contains zero and is closed under isomorphisms, finite biproducts and direct summands; $P$ has values in $\mathcal F$; $\epsilon$ is epimorphic). No additivity or preservation of zero morphisms of $P$ is needed. We obtain a preadditive category $C$ with a zero object and finite coproducts, a fully faithful additive functor $\iota:C\to A$ with $\iota(X)\in\mathcal F$ for every object $X$ of $C$, a zero-preserving functor $Q:A\to C$, and an epimorphic natural transformation $\pi:\iota Q\Rightarrow\operatorname{id}_A$.

source.place: Proof, first three sentences: reduction of the cover class to a zero-preserving left-resolution datum.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-left-resolution-bounded-minus] to $A,C,\iota,Q,\pi$ from step 1, whose hypotheses are exactly the conclusions of step 1. It supplies one functor $S$ on the full bounded-above subcategory and one natural augmentation $a:S\Rightarrow\iota_-$, so maps between complexes with different upper bounds are handled by the same functor. Every $a_L$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and every upper bound $b$ of $L$ is an upper bound of $S(L)$, which is the item's bound clause. Every term of $S(L)$ is isomorphic to $\iota(X)$ for some object $X$ of $C$; by step 1, $\iota(X)\in\mathcal F$, so the term lies in $\mathcal F$ because $\mathcal F$ is closed under isomorphisms. This gives the statement.

lean.statement: theorem exists_functorial_boundedAbove_class_resolution {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] (F : ObjectProperty A) [F.ContainsZero] [F.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms] (h_biproduct : ∀ (U V : A), F U → F V → F (U ⊞ V)) (h_summand : ∀ (U V : A), F (U ⊞ V) → F U ∧ F V) (P : A ⥤ A) (hP : ∀ (M : A), F (P.obj M)) (ε : P ⟶ 𝟭 A) (hε : ∀ (M : A), Epi (ε.app M)) : ∃ (S : CochainComplex.Minus A ⥤ CochainComplex A ℤ) (a : S ⟶ CochainComplex.Minus.ι A), (∀ (L : CochainComplex.Minus A), QuasiIso (a.app L)) ∧ (∀ (L : CochainComplex.Minus A) (i : ℤ), F ((S.obj L).X i)) ∧ (∀ (L : CochainComplex.Minus A) (b : ℤ), L.obj.IsStrictlyLE b → (S.obj L).IsStrictlyLE b)
